solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 28 across to 27); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Habit of Conservative Member of Parliament

parts.note: a group of owls is called a parliament, so one owl is a member of it

explanation.surface: A Tory MP's customary behaviour, or perhaps what they wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member of Parliament' looks like an MP but means a bird: a gathering of owls is a 'parliament'.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a monk's robe, and the hooded garment a monk wears is also called by this name.

clue.text: Brand ten exercises for a female "inspiring"

parts.note: to brand something is to label or call it
IO looks like the figures 1 and 0, making ten
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Branding ten workouts as aimed at women is billed as inspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ten' as IO is a crossword convention: the letters resemble the digits 10.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope is the Muse of epic poetry, one of the nine goddesses who inspire artists.

clue.text: Go after sort of current trendy wallpaper style

parts.note: to woo someone is to go after them romantically
DC, direct current, is one sort of electric current
hip means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: Chasing whatever is currently fashionable in wall coverings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'up to date' but is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: A textured wallpaper with small fragments of wood embedded in it, popular for decorating walls.

clue.text: Animal in OT reincarnated three times as lamb

indicators.note: reincarnated means brought back in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word as written out three times over

explanation.surface: An Old Testament beast returns in a new life, three times over, as a lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reincarnated' rearranges ASASAS (the word 'as' three times) plus LAMB.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Numbers, the prophet Balaam's donkey sees an angel and speaks to its master: a famous Old Testament animal.

clue.text: Maybe take constitutional risk, deposing leader

indicators.note: deposing the leader removes the first letter

parts.note: to gamble is to risk

explanation.surface: A political risk: changing the constitution by removing the head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constitutional' looks political but is a walk taken for health.
explanation.definitionFit: A constitutional is a leisurely walk for one's health, and a slow stroll is one way to take it.

clue.text: Type appearing in drag, topless or nude

indicators.note: appearing in means showing up inside, so this piece goes inside the other
topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to haul is to drag
nature means type or kind, as in things of that nature

explanation.surface: A performer in drag strips off the top, ending up naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag' is not cross-dressing but pulling: 'topless' beheads it and 'appearing in' sets the type inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: French for in the natural state, used in English to mean naked.

clue.text: Film competition different university runs internally

indicators.note: internally means placed inside the rearranged letters
different means changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A film competition at another university is run in-house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges COMPETITION, and 'internally' places U and R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for a cinema film, chiefly American and dated.

clue.text: Sort of race gear a bicycle needs

indicators.note: the phrase needs these letters within it, so they sit inside the clue words

explanation.surface: A kind of race where riders need a geared bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of race' is not a cycling event but a people: Arab ethnicity.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabic describes the Arab peoples, so in older usage it denotes a kind of race.

clue.text: Cockney sulks when opening number's ending

indicators.note: opening means going into, so this piece splits the number open

parts.note: six is a number

indicators.note: Cockneys drop their initial H, so that letter goes

parts.note: a huff is a sulk, and to huff is to sulk

explanation.surface: A Londoner sulks when a number finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys famously drop their aitches, so 'Cockney' removes the H; 'opening' puts the rest inside the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A suffix is a word ending added to make a new form, such as -ness.

clue.text: Young politician touring at the appropriate time, briefly

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the politician's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: LIB is short for a Liberal politician

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: on cue means at exactly the right moment

explanation.surface: A youthful politician goes on tour, arriving punctually and keeping it short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the last letter of ON CUE; 'touring' wraps the Liberal round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Young as a noun means offspring, and a baby big cat is one such youngster.

clue.text: Kind of pacifist, moderate at first, then consumed with rage

parts.note: CO is a conscientious objector, a pacifist who refuses to fight

indicators.note: at first means the first letter of the word

parts.note: passion means rage or strong anger
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A type of pacifist who is mild at first but then flies into a fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' looks like the start of a description, but 'Kind' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kind means showing sympathy and caring concern for others.

clue.text: Tie to be broadcast: semi, indeed

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a knot is a tie in a rope
semi- means half

explanation.surface: A sports fixture, a semi-final, is going to be televised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be broadcast' turns KNOT into its sound-alike NOT. The answer is British slang for emphatic agreement: 'Did you enjoy it?' 'Not half!'
explanation.definitionFit: British colloquial exclamation meaning very much so, used just as 'indeed' strengthens a reply.

clue.text: Post holder's description of US bodies — I hesitate to say: corrupt

parts.note: Inc, short for incorporated, is how American companies are described
um is the sound of hesitation
bent is slang for corrupt or dishonest

explanation.surface: An official who calls American institutions corrupt, if somewhat hesitantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US bodies' are corporations, which carry the label Inc.
explanation.definitionFit: The current occupant of an office or post is called its incumbent.

clue.text: Small antelope in pen recoiling before one

indicators.note: recoiling means springing back, so the pen's letters run backwards

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, from its inventor's name
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A little antelope in an enclosure shies away from somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like an enclosure for the antelope but is a ballpoint, which 'recoiling' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: The oribi is a small, slender African antelope of the grasslands.

clue.text: What has fellow worker maybe initially helping poor?

definitions.text: What has fellow worker maybe initially helping poor?

parts.note: Phil is a man's name, so a fellow
a worker ant is an example of a worker, hence maybe

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: ropy is British slang for poor in quality

explanation.surface: A question: what kind of colleague helps the needy?
explanation.walkthrough: 'ropy' is British informal for shoddy or poor. The whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable giving to help others, especially the poor, is the practice of benevolence the clue asks about.

clue.text: A second drinks order?

definitions.meaning: a moment, as in 'I'll be there in a jiffy'
a request for a pair of milkshakes

explanation.surface: Ordering another round at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Two shakes of a lamb's tail is a very short time, and a pair of milkshakes is what one would order.

clue.text: Object after this rustic Johnny finally gets old harvester's job?

indicators.note: after puts the synonym for object behind the other letters
finally means the last letter of each of the three words before it

parts.note: a thing is an object

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin grows old doing his farm work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the last letters of 'this rustic Johnny', giving SCY. The question mark flags that 'harvester' is a person mowing by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting crops with a long curved blade was the traditional work of a farmhand at harvest.

clue.text: An easy target, but donor's unsettled

parts.note: bar means but or except

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word donor, its 's being the verb is

explanation.surface: An easy mark, yet the giver is uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' rearranges DONOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying someone couldn't hit a barn door means they miss the biggest, easiest target.

clue.text: School audio plays without children's initial agreement, ironically

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
plays means performs freely, so these letters are rearranged
initial means the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A school's sound system plays its recordings, though the children did not agree first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' rearranges SCHOOL AUDIO, and 'without' wraps it around C, the initial of 'children's'. The phrase is old British slang meaning 'certainly not'.
explanation.definitionFit: This British catchphrase sounds like a yes but is used sarcastically to mean no way, an ironic assent.

clue.text: Rally, in short, not taking the rehearsed route

indicators.note: in short means cut off at the end, losing the last letter

parts.note: to rally is to recover or get better

explanation.surface: A short motor rally that avoids the practised course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rally' looks like a motor race but means to get better.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvisation, especially in theatre or comedy, is performing without a script, so unrehearsed.

clue.text: Drug crime stopped by volunteers over time

indicators.note: stopped by means plugged, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing, a crime
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers halted a drugs crime after some time.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A class of medicine taken to lower blood cholesterol.

clue.text: Saw underneath wheels, removing front

indicators.note: wheels means turns round, so the letters are read backwards
removing front means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: the bottom is what lies underneath

explanation.surface: A saw sits beneath a vehicle's wheels with its front piece taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a tool or a verb but is a saying. 'removing front' cuts BOTTOM to OTTOM, and 'wheels' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, the same kind of maxim as a guiding slogan.

clue.text: Back America to beat much of India

parts.note: hind means back or rear, as in hind legs
US is short for the United States of America
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: Supporting the United States in thrashing a large part of the Indian team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tan' is informal for to thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically the name for northern India, or the subcontinent broadly, so a large part of the country.

clue.text: Impossible, raising leg weight

indicators.note: raising, in a down clue, sends the letters upwards, so they read backwards

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Lifting a heavy weight with a leg can't be done.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially, something unacceptable or out of the question.

clue.text: Paparazzi sneak forwards

parts.note: a rat is a sneak or informer
in rugby the forwards are collectively the pack

explanation.surface: Press photographers creep forward to get their shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forwards' looks like a direction but is the rugby term: the forwards make up the scrum, called the pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabloid photographers who hunt celebrities in a crowd are disparagingly called by this name.

clue.text: Italian city is situated in plain to the west

indicators.note: situated in means placed inside, so the small word sits inside the synonym
in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: overt means plain, open to view

explanation.surface: An Italian town lies on a plain toward the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like flat land but means obvious. 'to the west' reverses OVERT to TREVO, and 'situated in' places the two letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Treviso is a city in the Veneto region of north-east Italy, near Venice.

clue.text: Head boy left to squeal: he was out for the count

definitions.text: he was out for the count

parts.note: the van is the front or head of an army or procession
he is the pronoun for a male, so a boy
to sing is slang for informing, as to squeal is

explanation.surface: A head boy has gone off to tell tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out for the count' suggests a knockout, but the count is Dracula, whom Bram Stoker's vampire hunter pursues.
explanation.definitionFit: Professor Abraham Van Helsing hunts Count Dracula in Bram Stoker's novel, so he was out to get him.

clue.text: Jelly range confectioner ultimately wanted

parts.note: an Aga is a make of British kitchen range cooker

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A confectioner finally needed a cooker to set the jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy cast-iron stove found in many British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: A gelatinous substance from seaweed used to set foods and grow cultures, so a kind of jelly.
